refs.title: Lie bracket of DequanLi and Blasius, by autoLie

history.origin: [DequanLi, Blasius] · a Lie bracket of two dysts systems
text: This is neither system. It is the Lie bracket of two of them, [f, g] = (∂f/∂x) g − (∂g/∂x) f, with f the DequanLi flow and g the Blasius flow, at their published parameters. The bracket measures how far the two flows fail to commute: follow f then g for a moment, then f and g backwards, and you miss where you started by an amount proportional to [f, g].
f — DequanLi: Related to the Three Scroll unified attractor TSUCS-2 Li, Phys Lett A. 2008: 387-393.
g — Blasius:  A chaotic food web composed of interacting predators,, consumers, and vegetation. Blasius, Huppert, Stone. Nature 1999
Its own flow is chaotic: nearby particles separate at roughly e^0.06 per crossing of the attractor.

The bracket was traced to closed form, printed as GLSL, and checked against autoLie's autograd bracket on the attractor (agreement to 4e-16). [g, f] is the same field reversed: the same curves, run backwards, so its attractors are this one's repellers.

refs.title: Lie bracket of Lorenz and Rossler, by autoLie

history.origin: [Lorenz, Rossler] · a Lie bracket of two dysts systems
text: This is neither system. It is the Lie bracket of two of them, [f, g] = (∂f/∂x) g − (∂g/∂x) f, with f the Lorenz flow and g the Rossler flow, at their published parameters. The bracket measures how far the two flows fail to commute: follow f then g for a moment, then f and g backwards, and you miss where you started by an amount proportional to [f, g].
f — Lorenz: A minimal weather model based on atmospheric convection. Lorenz, Edward N (1963). Deterministic nonperiodic flow. Journal of the atmospheric sciences 20.2 (1963): 130-141.
g — Rossler: Spiral-type chaos in a simple oscillator model. Rossler, O. E. (1976), An Equation for Continuous Chaos, Physics Letters, 57A (5): 3972013398,

Neither [f, g] nor [g, f] has a bounded attractor at these parameters: from every seed tried, particles either escape to infinity or stall at a fixed point. What you see is the field's flow near f's attractor, each particle re-seeded there once it runs away. When f and g both have constant divergence, as Lorenz and most of Sprott's systems do, the bracket is volume-preserving and cannot have an attractor at all.

The bracket was traced to closed form, printed as GLSL, and checked against autoLie's autograd bracket on the attractor (agreement to 4e-16). [g, f] is the same field reversed: the same curves, run backwards, so its attractors are this one's repellers.
